title: Dedicated enterprise intake: SLA & scaling heuristics for GPU-class and reserved throughput
creator: Carlos Nguyen
description: Problem: We receive varied enterprise requests for Dedicated capacity with inconsistent information about SLA targets, required throughput, and hardware preferences. That ambiguity slows scoping, causes multiple back-and-forths with sales/solutions, and increases time-to-onboard. Goal: Produce a concise intake heuristic and prioritization guidance that lets sales/SEs and the intake team classify requests into 4 capacity profiles (pilot, small-reserve, production, mission-critical), recommend a GPU class range, and suggest scaling/burst policies and default SLA bands. Deliverables: 1) Intake heuristic doc + fillable form for SEs, 2) Prioritization rubric with scorecard, 3) Default GPU-class recommendations and rationale, 4) Suggested autoscaling policies and burst allowances per profile, 5) Example customer triage walkthroughs and communication templates. Success metrics: reduce average scoping time from request to estimate by 40%, reduce clarifying interactions per request by 60%, and enable 75% of intake requests to be auto-classified into a profile without engineering input.
acceptance_criteria: A concise intake form exists (one page) and is tested by 3 SEs in live intake calls
Prioritization rubric produces a stable score for a set of 10 historical requests used as a test corpus
GPU-class guidance maps to existing supported SKUs and includes fallback options
Suggested scaling/burst policies are compatible with Dedicated autoscaling constraints and default guardrails
Stakeholders (Sales, Solutions, Infra Eng, CS) sign off on the rubric and communication templates
notes_and_workflow: 2025-02-18 - Carlos: Kickoff — captured core problem and initial scope. Invited Sales, Solutions, Infra Eng, and Solutions Architect reps. Asked for historical intake examples.
2025-02-21 - Maya: Collected 12 historical intake tickets from SalesOps; preliminary clustering shows 4 natural buckets based on peak qps, latency SLO, and data isolation requirements.

2025-02-24 - Infra Eng (synchronous meeting): Discussed GPU class mapping. Consensus: map model types to a tiered GPU recommendation (A100/Tr4 for high-throughput low-latency; H100/T4 mixes for cost-sensitive production). Need to codify memory and KV cache requirements.

2025-02-26 - Carlos: Drafted initial rubric with weighted dimensions: peak concurrent requests (30%), latency SLO (25%), data sensitivity/regulatory (15%), budget/commitment (15%), ops maturity (15%). Shared for feedback.

2025-02-28 - Feedback from Solutions: Request clearer guidance on burst policies and preemption risk. Proposed default burst allowance of 20% above reserved throughput for 1 hour/day for pilot and small-reserve profiles; mission-critical gets reserved burst + SLA buy-up option.

2025-03-01 - Maya: Incorporated feedback and ran rubric on 10 historical cases; rubric classification matched expected onboarding track in 8/10 cases. Two mismatches flagged for ambiguous latency vs cost trade-offs — added clarifying prompts to intake form.

Next steps: 1) Finalize one-page intake form and embed into Zendesk/Notion template; 2) Author GPU mapping table with explicit SKU mappings and memory/KV cache guidelines; 3) Draft recommended autoscaling/burst policy defaults and failure/fallback messaging; 4) Schedule stakeholder sign-off 2025-03-07.
final_notes: Aim to keep the intake form short and decision-focused: if a request can be auto-classified 75% of the time, route to Standard Dedicated onboarding; otherwise mark for engineering scoping. Avoid hard guarantees for GPU SKU until infra validates via a lightweight capacity check.
